then.text: Every cahow fledgling counts. Thank you. Come back in spring and you might hear them calling at night: it sounds like a ghost with a head cold.
Collector Pell has had a word with himself, I hear, and your cahowl's a credit to the colony.
Take this. A longtail's feather, found on the cliff, not plucked. Longtails arrive in spring and are the first thing you notice about Bermuda.

else.text: A man's been prowling Nonsuch's shore with a net and a shifty look. Pell, I think. Out on the bar. Would you have a word? Politely, with creatures.

then.text: A cahowl! A real one, on your team. I haven't seen one on a lead before. She's beautiful. Look at the way she sulks.

else.text: Burrows all counted. Now: a cahowl. They come out at night on the grass round the island, shy as anything. Catch one, and show me.
Three burrow markers to check: the beach by the Moongate, the Dockyard shore, and the Crystal Caves path. Just have a look at each. No touching.
Morning. I'm counting cahows. They were thought extinct for about three hundred years. Then in 1951 a few turned up on a rock. Now there's a few hundred.
Would you check three burrow markers for me? I can't leave the nests. One by the beach, one on the Dockyard shore, one on the cave path.
Then, if you can find one of the cahowl, I'd like to see it. And keep an eye out for anyone with a net.

then.text: The burrow has been checked. The chick inside is snoring in a very small way.

else.text: You peer in with a torch. A grey chick looks back. It is one of the rarest seabirds on Earth and it looks deeply unimpressed.
A white marker stake and a hole in the ground. A bird is in there, sulking.

then.text: The burrow has been checked. The chick inside is snoring in a very small way.

else.text: The burrow's mouth is a perfect little arch of limestone. Inside, a cahow chick does the stare of a creature who has already outlived three centuries of rumours.
A white marker stake and a hole in the ground. A bird is in there, sulking.

then.text: The burrow has been checked. The chick inside is snoring in a very small way.

else.text: Two eggs' worth of fluff and a warden's tag. The burrow has a little baffle to keep the larger birds out. The chick is smug about this.
A white marker stake and a hole in the ground. A bird is in there, sulking.

bm_shorts.text: Bermuda shorts are proper business wear here, you know. Worn with a jacket, tie, knee socks and shoes. I do not think it is funny.
Every cruise passenger says it is funny. It is a little bit funny. I'll give them that.

bm_gombey.text: Gombeys dance at Christmas, Boxing Day and New Year. Masks, feathers, whistle, drum. My granddad's troupe, my dad's troupe, now mine.
You dance to the drum, not the tune. There is no tune. The drum is the tune.
The whips are for show, mostly. The kids always want to hold one. The kids never get one.

bm_kid.text: The sand's pink because of tiny shells. Teacher said. I told her it's because the beach is shy.
I've been told not to take a bucket of it home. I took a pocket's worth. It's in my sock.

bm_vendor.text: Bermuda cedar. The first colonists built ships out of it, you know. Whole thing nearly died out in the forties when a bug got in.
I carve a little cedar longtail bird, if you want one. Not for sale today, I'm having a moment with it.

bm_fisher.text: Fish chowder, proper Bermudian: fish, tomato, onion, thyme, a splash of black rum and a few drops of sherry peppers at the table.
The sherry peppers are a hot sauce steeped in sherry. Don't put in more than three drops. You will anyway.

bm_tourist.text: We have six hours ashore! The guide said Bermuda is in the Atlantic, nowhere near the Caribbean, and about a thousand kilometres off North Carolina.
I thought it'd be hot. It's lovely. It's also, I'm told, the northernmost coral reef in the world. A coral reef, in a jumper climate.

bm_home.text: The Brize Norton flight? Next one's whenever the weather and the RAF agree, which is rarely the same time.
Head home to RAF Brize Norton?

then.text: Right-o. Mind the gap on the way in.

else.text: Take your time. We'll be here.

bermuda_bureau.text: Welcome to the bureau de change. Local money in, sterling out, or the other way round. A small fee, and a very small queue.

bermuda_homebound.text: Heading back to the mainland? Passage to RAF Brize Norton can be arranged whenever you like. Bring your own sandwiches.
